points.resolution_note: The morphology the original steps encode is right — masu-stem + たて — and I am not overturning it. What cannot be encoded is its scope. The record's own nuance field states the restriction and hands over the counterexample: "Limita-se a poucos verbos consagrados de ações com resultado físico e perceptível; não se diz 食べたて, por exemplo", and its formation field names exactly three verbs (焼く, 作る, 洗う). ～たて is therefore lexical, not productive. The base enum is verb / i-adjective / na-adjective / noun / clause / any: there is no value meaning "a closed lexical set of production verbs", and `verb` asserts full productivity over every verb. Executed literally the sequence returns 焼きたて (fine, record-licensed) but also 食べたて — the form the record names as impossible — plus したて and きたて. The steps would therefore ship a generator licence to produce the single form this entry exists to warn against, which is F5 in its purest form. Narrowing is not expressible, so no variants are emitted. Nothing pedagogical is lost: the record's formation field already carries all three worked pairs (焼く→焼きたて, 作る→作りたて, 洗う→洗いたて) in prose for a human, and the の-linking to a noun (焼きたてのパン) that the original steps never covered either is named in steps_unavailable so a later pass with a lexical-scope mechanism can pick both up.
points.steps_unavailable: ～たて is lexically restricted and the base enum cannot say so. The morphology (masu-stem + たて) is correct, but the record limits the pattern to a few established production verbs and names its own counterexample: 食べたて is not said. Its formation field licenses only 焼く→焼きたて, 作る→作りたて, 洗う→洗いたて. The base enum has no value for a closed lexical verb set, so any `verb` sequence generates 食べたて, したて and きたて alongside the three good forms. No steps are emitted rather than ship that over-generation. Also not covered by any op: the の-linking used when ～たて qualifies a noun (焼きたてのパン).

points.resolution_note: Two defects, both real. (1) Critical, fixed: variant 2's token began with ない while its base op already produces the な-inclusive stem, so the sequence doubled the negative — to-nai-stem(書く) = 書かな, plus "ないつもりでした" = *書かなないつもりでした, and likewise *食べなないつもりでした, *しなないつもりでした, *こなないつもりでした. The declared example 書かないつもりでした was right, which is what hid it: the example did not follow from the steps. Token corrected to "いつもりでした", which is byte-for-byte what the direct sibling gram:tsumori already carries (to-nai-stem + "いつもりです" → 書かないつもりです) and matches gram:n3-nai-to ("いと"), gram:n3-mama ("いまま"), gram:n3-you-ni-2 ("いように"). (2) Minor, excluded: variant 3 (to-ta-form + つもりでした → 書いたつもりでした) is grammatical Japanese but is a different meaning. The record's formation field lists only dictionary form and Verbo-ない; 〜たつもりでした appears solely in the nuance field, and there it is explicitly separated — "eu achava que tinha feito (mas não tinha)", uma convicção equivocada, diferente do simples plano não realizado. A variant object has no meaning or label field, so the two senses cannot be kept apart inside `variants`; filed unmarked under a point labelled "eu pretendia / eu ia", a generator asked for "eu pretendia escrever" can emit 書いたつもりでした, which means "I was under the impression I had written it". Dropped and named in steps_unavailable. The two emitted variants now match the record's formation field exactly.

Variant 2 was to-nai-stem + "ないうちに" while to-nai-stem already yields the な-inclusive stem, so the sequence doubled the negative: to-nai-stem(降る) = 降らな, plus "ないうちに" = *降らなないうちに, and likewise *書かなないうちに, *食べなないうちに, *しなないうちに, *こなないうちに. Its declared example 降らないうちに was correct and did not follow from its own steps. Token corrected to "いうちに", matching the sibling encodings of the same ない+particle shape: gram:n3-nai-to "いと", gram:n3-mama "いまま", gram:n3-you-ni-2 "いように". The branch itself is record-carried — the formation field says "Com verbo na negativa ない + うちに, expressa 'antes que (deixe de ser assim)'". The other five variants were re-executed and all hold: to-te-form + "いるうちに" gives 書いているうちに / 食べているうちに / しているうちに / きているうちに; to-te-form + "いないうちに" gives 書いていないうちに and the record's own 降っていないうちに; i-adjective + "うちに" gives 高いうちに; na-adjective to-attributive + "うちに" gives 静かなうちに, matching the record's "adjetivo な + な + うちに"; noun + "のうちに" gives 学生のうちに, matching "substantivo + の + うちに". The i-adjective example is set to 高いうちに (a mandated test base) rather than an adjective the record never mentions.
